title: Agent Service Manifest
description: A standardized descriptor for AI service value — pricing, quality, SLA, payment, and verification. v0.3 adds receipt_endpoint, verification, updated_at, and ttl for Signed Receipts integration and manifest freshness.

service_id.description: Globally unique service identifier. Recommended format: <provider>/<service>@<version>

provenance.description: Source and verification metadata for the manifest claims. Agents and reviewers use this to decide whether pricing, quality, SLA, and payment fields are fresh and independently checkable.

source_url.description: Primary URL used to derive or verify this manifest.

retrieved_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the source was retrieved.

last_verified_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the manifest claims were last checked against the source.

verification_status.description: Verification level for the manifest claims.

notes.description: Free-form reviewer notes, caveats, or verification context.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last manifest update. Agents use this to assess data freshness and detect stale manifests.

ttl.description: Time-to-live in seconds. Indicates how long this manifest can be cached before re-fetching. 0 = always re-fetch. Recommended: 3600 (1 hour) for stable services, 300 (5 min) for volatile pricing.

verified_by.description: List of entities that have verified this provider

description.description: Human-readable description of what the service does

functions.description: Concrete capabilities the tool offers, for task-fit matching (e.g. reminders, recurring_tasks, calendar_view, pomodoro_timer, natural_language_capture, sub_tasks). Beyond modalities; this is what the tool can actually DO.

context_window.description: Maximum context window size in tokens (LLM-specific)

pricing.description: Pricing engine — supports multiple billing dimensions, tiered pricing, and conditional pricing

billing_dimensions.description: One or more billing dimensions. A single service can have multiple (e.g., LLM charges for both input and output tokens).

dimension.description: Billing dimension identifier. Recommended values include input_token, output_token, token, character, word, image, pixel, second, minute, request, gpu_second, byte, query, and custom; services may define domain-specific dimensions such as browser_minute, email, or ci_minute.

unit.description: Billing granularity. Recommended values include per_1, per_1K, and per_1M; services may define domain-specific units such as per_page, per_message, or per_1_gb_month.

cost_per_unit.description: Cost per unit in the specified currency

up_to.description: Upper bound for this tier (integer or 'unlimited')

cost_per_unit.description: Cost per unit within this tier

conditions.description: Conditional pricing (e.g., price doubles when context > 200K)

estimated.description: true = pricing is an estimate (e.g., GPU-based models with variable runtime)

evaluated_at.description: Date when the evaluation was performed

self_reported.description: Whether this metric is self-reported by the provider (true) or independently verified (false)

cold_start.description: Cold start time for GPU-based models (e.g., '~15s')

payment.description: Payment methods and authentication — pre-wired for AP2 interop

methods.description: Supported payment methods. Recommended values include api_key_prepaid, stripe, ap2, crypto, invoice, and free_tier; services may declare platform-specific methods.

auth_type.description: Authentication mechanism required. Recommended values include api_key, oauth2, ap2_mandate, and none; services may declare platform-specific mechanisms.

ap2_endpoint.description: AP2 protocol merchant endpoint (if AP2 is supported)

receipt_endpoint.description: Endpoint URL for Signed Receipts (IETF ACTA). After service execution, agents POST to this endpoint to obtain a cryptographically signed receipt proving actual delivery metrics. Enables the ASM trust delta: |declared - actual| / declared.

receipt_envelope_version.description: Latest receipt envelope schema version this service emits and consumes. v0.1 spec at schema/asm-receipt-envelope-v0.1.schema.json. Optional; absence implies the consumer does not yet accept envelope-formatted receipts and falls back to the legacy ACTA POST.

delegates_to_supported.description: Whether receipts emitted by this service may carry a 'delegates_to' attribution chain. Pipelines that wrap sub-services (e.g. agentic IDEs delegating to upstream LLMs) SHOULD set this to true so consumers can resolve the full cost stack.

receipt_types.description: Defines the ASM-namespaced receipt types this service supports. These types appear in the 'type' field of ACTA signed receipt payloads.

asm:service_selection.description: Receipt issued when an agent selects this service. Captures selection provenance for audit.

declared_sla.description: Snapshot of declared SLA at selection time (latency, uptime, etc.)

selection_reasoning.description: Scorer output explaining why this service was chosen

roster_snapshot.description: List of service_ids that were available candidates at selection time. Enables auditors to verify the selection was made from the declared pool, not a restricted set.

verification.description: Verification configuration for Signed Receipts integration. Enables agents to verify receipt authenticity and establish computable trust.

protocol.description: Verification protocol used. 'signed-receipts-acta' = IETF ACTA Signed Receipts (recommended), 'w3c-vc' = W3C Verifiable Credentials, 'custom' = provider-specific.

public_key.description: Ed25519 public key as 64-character lowercase hex string. Compatible with the --key flag in npx @veritasacta/verify. Agents use this for offline receipt signature verification without contacting the receipt endpoint.

public_key_url.description: URL to fetch the public key (alternative to inline public_key). Supports key rotation.

receipt_schema_version.description: Version of the receipt schema this service produces (e.g., '1.0')

operational_constraints.description: Experimental pre-call operational envelope for client policy decisions: risk class, side effects, approval boundaries, spend caps, quotas, rate limits, and receipt expectations. Draft v0.4 field accepted in v0.3.x for producer-side adoption trials; clients enforce local policy.

risk_class.description: Coarse operational risk level declared by the publisher or curator.

side_effects.description: Declared side effects such as read_only, external_api_call, persistent_state, financial_charge, sends_message, executes_code, or network_access.

approval.description: Pre-call approval envelope. ASM exposes policy inputs; clients decide whether and how to enforce them.

required.description: Whether this service requires approval before invocation.

conditions.description: Human-readable or implementation-defined conditions that trigger approval.

spend_caps.description: Publisher-declared or recommended spend boundaries. Consumer policy remains authoritative.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code for the spend caps.

quotas.description: Provider quota envelope, usually daily or monthly.

rate_limits.description: Provider request-rate envelope, usually per second, minute, or hour.

receipt_required.description: Whether clients should expect a post-call receipt before updating trust.

invocation.description: How (and whether) an autonomous agent can actually drive this tool — the primary eligibility gate for agent tool selection. Distinct from payment/auth: this answers 'can the agent operate it at all, and from where', not 'who pays'.

interface.description: Primary machine interface. Recommended values: rest_api, graph_api, graphql, grpc, mcp, sdk, cli, url_scheme, applescript, shortcuts, webhook, gui, none.

reach.description: cloud = a remote/headless agent can call it from anywhere; local_device = only an agent running on the user's own machine/OS can drive it (e.g. AppleScript or Shortcuts); hybrid = both.

agent_operable.description: Whether an autonomous agent can drive the tool end-to-end without a human in the loop, in the appropriate reach environment.

auth_to_invoke.description: Credential needed to invoke. Recommended values: none, api_token, oauth, account_login, device_local, byo_key.

agent_completable_setup.description: Whether an agent can get from zero to a working call with NO human-in-the-loop step. False if the tool requires a signup, payment, OAuth consent, or manual approval the agent cannot complete unattended — even if it technically accepts credentials once a human has set it up. Distinguishes 'immediately usable' from 'usable only after human onboarding'.

setup_requires.description: Human-in-the-loop onboarding steps required before an agent can invoke. Recommended values: free_api_key_signup, paid_signup, oauth_consent, manual_approval, licensing_agreement, account_creation, api_key_request. Empty or absent means immediately usable with no human step.

automation_paths.description: For non-cloud or GUI tools, concrete automation hooks an agent could use, e.g. applescript, shortcuts, url_scheme, computer_use.

platforms.description: OS/ecosystem where the tool runs or is operable. Recommended values: web, macos, ios, windows, android, linux, any.

usage_terms.description: Whether and how an agent is permitted to use the service, independent of whether it is technically reachable. A tool may expose an API yet forbid automated use, or be GUI-only yet explicitly bless scripting.

automation_allowed.description: Whether the Terms of Service permit automated / agent-driven use.

license.description: License or usage tier governing programmatic use.

data_governance.description: What happens to data the agent puts into or pulls from the service: ownership, portability, training use, retention, residency. The consequences-of-use class an agent must weigh on a human's behalf.

data_owner.description: Who owns data created or submitted through the service.

exportable.description: Whether the user can export / take their data out.

trains_on_user_data.description: Whether the provider uses user data to train its models.

residency.description: Data residency regions, e.g. us, eu.

lock_in_notes.description: Switching cost, proprietary-format, or portability caveats.

extensions.description: Category-specific non-standard fields, isolated by namespace. Core schema remains stable; all domain-specific data goes here.
